title: Best Samsung Fast Chargers
short: USB-C GaN chargers compared by wattage, ports and Samsung Super Fast Charging (PPS) support.
intro: Most Samsung Galaxy phones do not come with a charger in the box, and not every USB-C charger actually delivers full speed to a Galaxy phone. This guide compares GaN chargers tested by Android Authority, and explains the PPS detail that determines whether you get Samsung's fastest charging speed.

products.name: Nano 3 30W GaN Charger
products.best_for: Everyday charging for one Galaxy phone
products.summary: A compact, affordable single-port charger with foldable plug pins and PPS support for Samsung fast charging. Android Authority notes the device can get warm during charging.
cons: Device can get warm while charging

products.name: Prime 67W GaN Wall Charger
products.best_for: Buyers who want to charge a phone and other devices from one charger
products.summary: Android Authority's overall pick. It balances power and portability across three ports, supports Samsung fast charging and is highly efficient, though it costs more than single-port options.

products.name: Prime 100W GaN Wall Charger
products.best_for: Charging a Galaxy phone and a laptop from the same charger
products.summary: A powerful, compact charger that can run multiple devices including laptops, with strong efficiency, though it is expensive and Android Authority notes the newer model has reduced efficiency versus the original.

products.name: Enercore CJ11 67W
products.best_for: Travellers who want a charger and cable in one unit
products.key_spec: 67W, built-in retractable cable plus 2 USB-C ports
products.summary: A compact travel charger with a built-in retractable cable alongside two USB-C ports. It is not powerful enough for demanding laptops.
cons: Not enough power for demanding laptops

products.name: Nexode 500W 6-Port Desktop Charger
products.best_for: Households or desks charging several phones and laptops at once
products.summary: A desktop charging station that can power several laptops and phones at once with wide protocol support, including Samsung fast charging. It is expensive, heavy and oversized for a single user.

products.name: 45W Travel Adapter
products.best_for: Buyers who want a first-party charger guaranteed to work correctly
products.summary: Samsung's own 45W charger, which Android Authority calls a surprisingly affordable first-party option with full PPS support for Samsung fast charging.
pros: Surprisingly affordable for a first-party charger

products.name: Nexode RG 30W
products.best_for: Buyers who want a low-cost single-port charger with PPS
products.summary: A power-efficient single-port charger with the essential features covered and PPS support, though Android Authority found its dot-matrix screen more gimmick than useful.
cons: Dot-matrix screen is more gimmick than useful

products.name: USB-C 130W GaN
products.badge: Best for travelling with a phone and laptop
products.best_for: Buyers who want one charger for a Galaxy phone, a laptop and more on the go
products.summary: A high-power multi-port charger with swappable international prongs, useful for anyone travelling with a Galaxy phone and a laptop who wants to pack one charger instead of several.

guide.q: Why does my Samsung phone charge slowly with a 'fast' charger?
guide.a: Samsung's fastest charging speeds require the charger to support PPS (Programmable Power Supply), not just a high wattage number. A 45W charger without PPS can drop a Galaxy phone to a much slower speed, so check PPS support specifically rather than just the wattage on the box.

guide.q: What wattage charger do I need for my Galaxy phone?
guide.a: Most Galaxy phones charge at up to 25W or 45W depending on the model. Buying a higher-wattage charger than your phone needs does not damage it or speed it up beyond your phone's own limit, but it is useful if you also want to charge a tablet or laptop from the same charger.

guide.q: Is a GaN charger worth paying more for?
guide.a: GaN (gallium nitride) chargers run cooler and are significantly smaller and lighter than older silicon chargers of the same wattage, which makes them worth it if you travel or want a compact charger for a bag.

guide.q: Is it safe to buy an unbranded cheap charger?
guide.a: Any charger sold in the UK should carry UKCA or CE marking as a minimum safety requirement. Unbranded imports without this marking have not been independently verified for UK mains safety, so it is worth sticking to established brands.
